listenings.text: Hey guys, it's Kai. Quick update about Saturday. The forecast for Trigg is two meters with a strong onshore wind, so that's too big and too messy for most of us. Forget it. We're going south instead, to the beach break near the lighthouse. It's about an hour in the car, and it's smaller, about one meter, with an offshore wind until ten. Perfect. We need rides. Jess's dad has a van, but it isn't big enough for everybody and all the boards, so we need one more car. If your mum or dad can drive, tell me tonight. Meet at the school parking lot at half past five. Not six. Half past five. And bring enough water and food for the whole morning, because there's no shop there. Nothing. See you Saturday.

Hi love, it's Bev. I got your message about Saturday. So, yes, you can go, but I have three conditions. First, you're not old enough to drive, and neither are your mates, so an adult drives. Jess's dad is fine. Second, Kai says the waves are small enough, and I believe him, but you are not surfing on your own. Ever. Stay close to the group. The currents on that coast are strong, and you don't know the beach well enough yet. And third, it's winter here, love. The water is colder than you think. Take your long wetsuit, and a warm jacket for after. You were too cold on Tuesday and you didn't say anything. I saw your lips. They were blue. Right. Have fun.

reading.rtitle: The Boardriders' Beach Guide: where do we go this Saturday?
paras: Every Saturday the club goes somewhere different, and the first question is always the same: where? The answer is never the biggest waves. It is the best waves for the group. A beach that is perfect for our strongest surfers can be too dangerous for somebody in their first month, and a beach that is easy for a beginner is often not interesting enough for everybody else.

Our home beach is fine on most days, but when the wind turns onshore after ten in the morning, the water gets choppy and the waves close out. That is why we go early. If you arrive at eleven, you are too late. There are also too many people on a Saturday, and a crowded line-up is not a good place to learn.

The reef at the point is the best wave near the city when the swell is big enough, but it is shallow at low tide and the rocks are close. It is only for experienced surfers, and only with somebody who knows it. If you have to ask if you are good enough for the reef, the answer is: not yet.

Our favorite trip is the beach break an hour south. It is quieter, the waves are softer, and in the morning the wind is often offshore, so the water is glassy. There is one problem: there is a strong current near the rocks at the north end. Stay in the middle of the beach and stay close to the group. And there is no shop, so bring enough food and water for the whole morning.

items.situation: Kai asks if you want to surf the reef at the point. It is three meters today. Say no, and say why.
The waves at your home beach are tiny today. Tell the group, and suggest another beach.
Jess's dad's van is full. Explain the problem to your host mum and ask her for a ride.
Now you are the captain. A new member wants to paddle out at the north end, near the rocks. Stop him, politely.
After the trip, your mum in Brazil asks how it was. Say one thing that was too much and one thing that was not enough.
